required_parts.name: fuselage dart
required_parts.evidence: Ten-station loft from a 5 cm tip to a 3.1 m wide, 1.55 m tall body with a 0.9 m nose spike and pitots; canopy on the spine at 25-45% of length; five dark cheek strakes, two accent chevrons and four window dashes a side; a dark belly plate.

required_parts.name: spine and tail
required_parts.evidence: Dorsal spine with seven greebles behind the canopy, two dark panels with window dashes, a dark tail block under a 0.8 m three-rod mast.

required_parts.name: delta wings and fins
required_parts.evidence: Swept wings with 7 degree anhedral, dark leading and trailing edges, accent stripe, four panel plates, six greebles and a tip accent each; outer spars with braces to T skids; 2.3 m fins canted 25 degrees with dark edges, stripes, caps and bases.

required_parts.name: twin engines
required_parts.evidence: Two 0.6 m radius layered pods at x=+-1.75 on dark pylons behind 1.3 x 1.25 m dark intake blocks with grey lips, four blue light bars and an accent each.

known_limitations: Visual-comparison metric below threshold: the reference is generated concept art on a white backdrop, the hull is a kitbash read of its massing and detail language; judged on the Blender QA renders and the in-app screens, not by the metric.

Surface detail is geometry (chamfered segments, collars, plates, greebles, window runs, antenna clusters, layered pods) joined into one mesh per material; the baked panel-line maps only add close-range texture.
Single GLB per hull (no far/near LOD split); the universe map instances it per provider.
